    [Algebra k X.functionField] [IsConstantField k X] (U₀ U₁ : X.Opens)

/-- **The geometric principal-degree-zero statement, reduced to residue degree
one.**  `Σ_P ord_P(g) = 0` follows from the closed ledger together with
`[κ(P):k] = 1` on the support of `div g`.

This makes the reduction of the open leaf `Scheme.WeilDivisor.principal_degree_zero`
machine-checked rather than merely asserted: the *whole* remaining content of that
leaf, given the ledger, is the residue-degree-one fact for a smooth proper curve
over an algebraically closed field.  It is stated here on the adelic hypotheses
(`Algebra k K(X)`, `IsConstantField`, a 2-affine cover, the ledger) rather than on
the leaf's own geometric hypotheses, which is why it does not literally close that
`sorry` — the missing step is instantiating these hypotheses from
`[IsProper] [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1] [GeometricallyIrreducible]` over `k̄`,
together with `residueDeg k̄ P = 1`. -/
theorem degree_principal_eq_zero_of_residueDeg_eq_one
    (hledger : ∀ D : X.WeilDivisor, chi k U₀ U₁ D = chi k U₀ U₁ 0 + degK k D)
    {g : X.functionField} (hg : g ≠ 0)
    (h1 : ∀ P ∈ (show X.PrimeDivisor →₀ ℤ from
      Scheme.WeilDivisor.principal g hg).support, residueDeg k P = 1) :
    Scheme.WeilDivisor.degree (Scheme.WeilDivisor.principal g hg) = 0 := by
  rw [← degK_eq_degree_of_residueDeg_eq_one k h1]
  exact degK_principal_eq_zero k U₀ U₁ hledger hg

end GeometricDegree

/-! ## §4. `degK_principal_eq_zero` versus the geometric `principal_degree_zero`

`degK_principal_eq_zero` above and the open leaf
`Scheme.WeilDivisor.principal_degree_zero` are **different statements**, and the
first does not imply the second.  Recorded here because the difference is easy to
misread as a formality.

* `degK_principal_eq_zero` concerns `deg_k (div g) = Σ_P ord_P(g)·[κ(P):k]`.  Its
  proof is the χ-transport of `ClassInvariance.lean` plus the closed ledger, and
  it is stated over an **arbitrary** base field of constants `k`.
* `principal_degree_zero` concerns the **unweighted** `Σ_P ord_P(g)`, and is
  stated on a smooth proper curve over an algebraically **closed** `k̄` with no
  field of constants in sight and no ledger hypothesis.

Over `k̄` the two degrees coincide because every closed point of a smooth curve has
residue field `k̄`, i.e. `[κ(P):k̄] = 1`.  That collapse is
`degK_eq_degree_of_residueDeg_eq_one`, and composing it with
`degK_principal_eq_zero` gives `degree_principal_eq_zero_of_residueDeg_eq_one`:
the **unweighted** statement, proved, from the ledger plus residue-degree-one.

So the reduction is machine-checked, and the residue of the open leaf is now **one** item,
not two.  Item 1 below is closed; item 2 is what remains.

1. `residueDeg k̄ P = 1` — **DISCHARGED**, in `Adelic/ResidueField.lean`
   (`residueDeg_eq_one_of_isAlgClosed_curve`), for a prime divisor of a curve
   `C : Over (Spec k̄)` with `k̄` algebraically closed, under
   `[IsIntegral] [IsLocallyNoetherian] [IsRegularInCodimensionOne] [LocallyOfFiniteType]`
   and `[SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1]` — all of which the project's headline curve already
   carries, `LocallyOfFiniteType` because mathlib's `IsProper` extends it structurally.

   (An earlier version of this sentence said `LocallyOfFiniteType` "synthesizes from
   smoothness".  **That is false in the relevant import closure**: the
   `SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 → Smooth` bridge lives in
   `AlgebraicJacobian/Curve/GeometricallyReduced.lean`, which `Adelic/ResidueField.lean` does
   not import, and `infer_instance` for `LocallyOfFiniteType` from smoothness alone fails

   unchanged, because `principal_degree_zero` and every other real consumer carries

theorem sectionSub_divisorOfList_replicate_of_notMem (U : X.Opens)
    {P : X.PrimeDivisor} (hP : P.point ∉ U) (E : X.WeilDivisor) (n : ℕ) :
    sectionSub k U (divisorOfList (List.replicate n P) + E) = sectionSub k U E := by
  induction n with
  | zero => simp only [List.replicate_zero, divisorOfList, zero_add]
  | succ m ih =>
    rw [List.replicate_succ]
    simp only [divisorOfList]
    rw [show pointDivisor P + divisorOfList (List.replicate m P) + E
          = pointDivisor P + (divisorOfList (List.replicate m P) + E) by abel,
      sectionSub_add_pointDivisor_of_notMem k U hP, ih]

Two of the three Čech terms are frozen by the tower and the third is trapped under the
overlap term (`Γ(U₁,−) ⊆ 𝒜`, antitonicity in the open).  No exactness hypothesis. -/
theorem chi_le_finrank_chart_along_tower (hcov : U₀ ⊔ U₁ = ⊤)

    [∀ D : X.WeilDivisor, Module.Finite k (sectionSub k U₀ D)]
    [∀ D : X.WeilDivisor, Module.Finite k (sectionSub k U₁ D)]
    [∀ D : X.WeilDivisor, Module.Finite k (sectionSub k (U₀ ⊓ U₁) D)]
    (n : ℕ) :
    chi k U₀ U₁ (divisorOfList (List.replicate n P) + E)
      ≤ (Module.finrank k (sectionSub k U₀ E) : ℤ) := by
  have hPinf : P.point ∉ (U₀ ⊓ U₁ : X.Opens) := fun h => hP h.1
  set D := divisorOfList (List.replicate n P) + E with hD
  have h := chi_eq_charts_sub_overlap k U₀ U₁ hcov D
  have hle : Module.finrank k (sectionSub k U₁ D)
      ≤ Module.finrank k (sectionSub k (U₀ ⊓ U₁) D) :=
    Submodule.finrank_mono (sectionSub_antitone_open k inf_le_right D)
  have h0 : sectionSub k U₀ D = sectionSub k U₀ E := by
    rw [hD]; exact sectionSub_divisorOfList_replicate_of_notMem k U₀ hP E n
  rw [h0] at h
  omega

/-- **Chart-level finiteness alone forbids Riemann growth: `ℓ` is BOUNDED along a tower.**

`ℓ(n·P + E) ≤ dim Γ(U₀, 𝒪(E))` for every `n`, whenever `P.point ∉ U₀` and the `U₀`-chart
section spaces are finite-dimensional.  No cover hypothesis, no χ, no exactness datum: it is

**This is the root cause of everything in §5–§6, and it is worth stating separately because it is
stronger and simpler than the χ-level statements.**  Riemann–Roch says `ℓ(D)` grows like
`deg D`; this says it *cannot*, along any tower at a point missing a chart whose sections are
finite-dimensional.  So `Module.Finite k (sectionSub k U D)` at a **non-total** `U` is not
bookkeeping — it is a substantive geometric restriction, and any theorem assuming it over all
divisors has already excluded the curves Riemann–Roch is about.

**How substantive was underestimated here, and the sharp form is not about towers at all.**  This
docstring says the binder "excludes the curves Riemann–Roch is about"; in fact it excludes *every*
curve with a nonconstant function, and needs neither a tower nor a cover to see it.  A single
instance at `D = 0` forces `K(X)/k` finite — `Γ(U,𝒪(0))` is a ring containing `Γ(X,U)`, a

**This entry previously said the opposite. Corrected 2026-07-28 (run 0074, task `ajc-rr`), in
Lean and kernel-checked.**

In `Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge`, the adelic Riemann–Roch lane
(`AlgebraicJacobian/RiemannRoch/Adelic/`) states most results conditional on the closed χ-ledger
`hledger : ∀ D, χ(D) = χ(0) + deg_k D` or the one-point bump `hbump`. `ChiUnconditional.lean`
carries refutations of both (`not_bump_of_notMem_left`, `ledger_refuted_of_notMem_left`), and the
old version of this note reported them as settling the matter, concluding "the cover is the
problem" and "find a cover excluding such primes".

**Both refutations run on `[∀ D, Module.Finite k (sectionSub k U₀ D)]` at a NON-TOTAL open, and
that binder is unsatisfiable on a curve.** `Adelic/ChartFinitenessRefuted.lean`: `sectionSub k U 0`
is a *ring* (orders add) containing `Γ(X,U)`; a `k`-finite domain is a field; a field between
`Γ(X,U)` and its own fraction field is all of `K(X)`. So one instance at `D = 0` alone forces
`K(X)/k` finite (`module_finite_functionField_of_chart_finite`), and the binder is *equivalent* to
that (`chart_finiteness_iff_module_finite_functionField`). `K(X)/k` is never finite once a single
prime divisor exists, since the DVR stalk would be a `k`-finite domain hence a field
(`not_module_finite_functionField_of_primeDivisor`).

So `hbump` and `hledger` are **OPEN at a curve, not false**, and the lane's `hledger`-conditional
results are **not** shown vacuous. The second refutation route
(`LedgerClosure.not_bump_of_notMem_overlap`) carries no chart-finiteness binder but rests on
`chi_add`'s four exactness data, which the lane never constructs — so it does not reach a curve
either, for a different reason.

affine `X` even the `⊤` binder collapses (`not_chart_finite_top_of_isAffine`), and

this argument does not apply — which is **not** the same as those `⊤` binders holding; that is
finiteness of `L(D)`, Riemann–Roch's own content, still open.

**How to apply:** do NOT hunt a better cover — there is none, and the two-chart count is squeezed
(unsatisfiable at affine charts, vacuous at `U₀=U₁=⊤` where the criterion becomes `ℓ=ℓ`). Replace
the two-chart adelic count rather than weakening its hypotheses. The route with evidence is the

name: refutation-with-unsatisfiable-hypotheses
description: A refutation whose own hypotheses are unsatisfiable at your object reports clean axioms and is TRUE, but closes nothing — check negative results by instantiation, like positive ones.
metadata:
  type: feedback
---

When a formalization proves `¬H` under binders `B`, the instinct is to treat the route through `H`
as closed. It is closed only if `B` is satisfiable **at the object you care about**. If not, the
refutation is true, axiom-clean, non-vacuous in the abstract — and says nothing.

This is the mirror of the more familiar trap (a theorem with a false hypothesis is vacuously true).
It is more dangerous, because a *negative* result normally reads as permission to stop: in
`Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge` it produced three rounds of argument, five docstrings and a roadmap
comment all directing the next session to solve a problem that did not exist
([[ajc-adelic-ledger-refuted]]). Filed as trap (i) in that project's
`scripts/axiom-frontier.lean` §2b/§6g.

**How to apply:**
- Instantiate a refutation's binders at your actual object before believing it closes a route.
  Elaborating a consumer is the test; reading the signature is not, because instantiability is
  also `open`-sensitive when producers are `scoped` instances.
- When you claim "nothing refutes X", enumerate the routes. Inferring "no route works" from "the
  route I analysed does not" is the same error one level up.
- **Retracting an overstatement is itself an opportunity to overstate.** Having withdrawn "the
  refutation is unconditional", the natural replacement — "so those hypotheses are fine / survive"
  — is equally unchecked. An absence of derivation is not a proof of safety. Say "not refuted by
  this route" and stop there.
